headline: Formal Verification Lets a 93-Line Spec Stand In for 1,000+ Lines of AI-Written Code
what_happened: Developer "schildep" published a formally verified 3D mesh-intersection library: a 93-line mathematical specification, in the Lean 4 proof language, that a human can read and trust, backing an implementation with over 1,000 lines of AI-generated code and 60,000-plus lines of AI-generated proofs. Lean's compiler automatically checks every proof against the spec, so reviewers never inspect the implementation itself. A WebAssembly browser demo lets users test it on sample meshes or their own STL files.
why_it_matters: It's a concrete answer to "how do you trust AI-written code": don't review the code at all, write a short, human-checkable spec and let a proof checker verify the AI's much larger implementation against it automatically, catching errors a manual code review would likely miss.
one_liner: A developer showed that instead of trying to read and trust thousands of lines of AI-written code, you can write a much shorter set of rules and have a computer prove the AI's code actually follows them.

citations.quote: trust 93 lines of spec, not 1000+ lines of AI-written code
